channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Kim vows to 'irreversibly' cement North Korea's nuclear status
item.description: In his speech, Kim expressed pride in the country's rapid expansion of nuclear weapons and missiles in recent years, calling it the "right" choice.

item.title: Senate confirms Sen. Mullin as DHS secretary. And, Iran denies U.S. talks to end war
item.description: The Senate has confirmed Markwayne Mullin as the next Department of Homeland Security secretary. And, Iran has denied that it's in talks with the U.S. to end the war, which is now in its fourth week.

item.title: Despite state bans and restrictions, the number of abortions in the U.S. holds steady
item.description: The Guttmacher Institute has a new analysis on how many abortions happened in 2025.

item.title: 'Lawmakers' Day 36: High school cellphone ban OK'd; Senate debates permanent daylight saving time
item.description: Lawmakers gave final passage to a bill banning cellphone use in high schools and debated making daylight saving time permanent.

item.title: ICE agents deploy to Atlanta airport to assist with security lines. The public's response is mixed
item.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents are now assisting with long security lines that stretched out the doors at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport early on Monday morning. ICE agents deploy to Atlanta airport to assist with security lines. The public's response is mixed

item.title: Iran fires more missiles at Israel and rejects Trump's talk as 'fake news' for markets
item.description: Israeli health officials said Iranian missiles struck four sites across Israel Tuesday, including central Tel Aviv, injuring at least six people. Iranian authorities also said a gas supply line in southwest Iran was struck overnight.

item.title: Trump takes aim at windmills despite increasing energy costs
item.description: President Trump's mission to fight renewable wind energy comes at a time of rising energy costs.

item.title: GPB morning headlines for March 24, 2026
item.description: As long security lines persist, passengers and airport staff are having a mixed response to the ICE agents now deployed at Atlanta’s Hartsfield Jackson International Airport; Nine original founding era documents from the National Archives arrived in Atlanta Monday; The Georgia Senate passed a bill that could make daylight savings time permanent in the state.

item.title: Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon
item.description: Pulido has been a mainstay of Tejano music —a genre blending traditional regional Mexican elements with country, pop and conjunto influences — for more than three decades.

item.title: Supreme Court appears skeptical of laws counting mail-in ballots after Election Day
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case that tests whether states should be allowed to count ballots that are mailed on time but arrive after Election Day. The case could have broad implications.

item.title: Trump delivers farmers another financial blow with Iran war
item.description: Some of President Trump's policies, the latest being the war in Iran, are testing his support among farmers who are being burdened with higher costs.

item.title: Lawmakers: Spotlight - Georgia Budget Explained: Tax Cuts, Surplus Spending, & What It Means for You
item.description: Georgia lawmakers break down the state’s amended and upcoming budgets, explaining how billions in tax revenue are allocated and what proposed income tax cuts could mean for your wallet. You’ll hear how education, mental health, and property tax relief are shaping spending priorities, along with insights into surplus funds and economic pressures. This episode helps you understand how state budget decisions directly impact your daily life in Georgia.

item.title: Pakistan is poised to host the U.S. and Iran for talks to end the war
item.description: The Pakistani prime minister said his country stands ready to host negotiations toward a settlement as the war with Iran nears the one-month mark.

item.title: Judge, expressing doubt on abortion murder charge, grants bond to Georgia mother
item.description: A Coastal Georgia district attorney and a Superior Court judge said Monday they were doubtful that enough evidence exists to move forward with a malice murder charge against a 31-year-old Camden County mother arrested earlier this month for an alleged illegal abortion, paving the way for a possible reduction or dismissal of charges.
